headline: Council may act on $200,000 from the Housing Trust Fund for the Champlain Housing Trust Dorset Commons project.
summary: The agenda covers the Dorset Commons housing request, a Chittenden County Regional Planning Commission report, housing trends and targets, and a housing action plan pilot. It also includes a vacant building and graffiti ordinance, Hubbard Park lights, and executive sessions on 1720 Spear Street and the Williston Road Pump Station.
items: Public comments on topics not on the agenda
Councilor announcements and City Manager's report
Consent agenda: sign disbursements (11-2-2026 AP warrant)
Consent agenda: approve application for FFY2026 State Homeland Security Grant for the Emergency Operations Plan
Consent agenda: authorize plowing agreements for 2026-2027 for private roadways dedicated to the City, and a wastewater maintenance agreement for the Spear Meadows neighborhood
Consent agenda: appoint Isaac Theodore Reicin to a 3-year term on the Development Review Board
Receive and possibly approve Housing Committee recommendation to allocate $200,000 from the Housing Trust Fund to the Champlain Housing Trust Dorset Commons project
Receive the Chittenden County Regional Planning Commission Annual Report
Council-requested conversation on housing trends and targets in the State, County, and City
Receive update on shared Housing Needs Assessment and Housing Action Plan Pilot with CCRPC and possibly endorse the approach
Receive Town Meeting TV Annual Report and budget presentation
Discuss Council priorities for the Legislative Advocacy Agenda
Council request: discuss goals for a vacant building and graffiti ordinance
Council request: discuss standardized communication to residents who contact the City Council and staff
Council request: discuss wildlife-friendly (amber) bulbs and hours of operation for lights at Hubbard Park
Council request: discuss an intended legal opinion on municipal authority to regulate building and thermal energy systems
Council request: discuss process and reporting improvements for high-value projects

Review significant agenda topics for the November 16, 2026 Council meeting: pension actuarial update, Library Board 5-year Strategic Plan, Legislative Advocacy Agenda for 2027-2028, and parking ticket fees and a Parking Fund
Other business: executive session on negotiation of real estate lease or purchase options for 1720 Spear Street
Other business: executive session on negotiation of real estate lease or purchase options for the Williston Road Pump Station
location: 180 Market Street, Main Floor, Auditorium (also available on Zoom)

City Council Meeting Agenda
November 2, 2026
Participation Options
l In Person: 6:30 PM | 180 Market Street, Main Floor, Auditorium 
l Assistive Listening Service Devices available upon request  
l Electronically: https://zoom.us/j/99047286923
Phone 929 205 6099 Webinar ID: 990 4728 6923
Pledge of Allegiance (6:30 pm)
Instructions on exiting building in case of emergency and review of technology options –
Jessie Baker, City Manager (6:31 pm)
Agenda Review: Additions, deletions or changes in order of agenda items (6:33 pm)
Comments and questions from the public not related to the agenda (6:35 pm)
Councilors’ Announcements and Reports on Committee assignments and City Manager’s 
Report (6:45 pm)
Consent Agenda (6:55-7:00 pm)
Consider and Sign Disbursements
6A. 11-2-2026 AP WARRANT.PDF
Approve the application for a FFY2026 State Homeland security Grant to assist in 
funding the City's Emergency Operations Plan
6B1. GRANT FORM FOR EMERGENCY OPERATIONS PLAN GRANT.PDF
6B2. GRANT GUIDANCE.PDF
Authorize the Director of Public Works to enter into plowing agreements for the 2026-
2027 year for private roadways which have been dedicated to the City for future 
acceptance. Further, authorize the Director of Public Works to enter into a wastewater 
maintenance agreement for the 2026-2027 year for the Spear Meadows neighborhood 
which has been dedicated to the City for future acceptance.
6C1. COVER SHEET - DPW PLOWING AGREEMENTS.PDF
6C2. PLOWING AGREEMENT TEMPLATES 2026.PDF
Appoint Isaac Theodore Reicin to serve a 3-year term on the Development Review Board
6D. COVER SHEET - DRB APPOINTMENT.PDF
Receive and possibly approve a Housing Committee recommendation that $200,000 be 
allocated from the Housing Trust Fund to the Champlain Housing Trust Dorset Commons 
project - Nora Senecal, Housing Committee Chair (7:00-7:15 pm)
7A. COVER SHEET - CHT REQUEST FOR DORSET COMMONS.PDF
7B. HTF CHT CC MEMO 2026-11-02.PDF
7C. HTF CHT RECOMMENDATION.PDF
Receive the Chittenden County Regional Planning Commission Annual Report - Charlie 
Baker, Executive Director (7:15-7:30 pm)
8A. COVER SHEET - CCRPC ANNUAL REPORT 2026.PDF
8B. SOUTHBURLINGTON_CCRPC_FY26_FINAL.PDF
Hold a Council-requested conversation on housing trends and targets in the State, County, 
and City - Charlie Baker, Executive Director, Paul Conner, Director of Planning & Zoning -
Charlie Baker, Executive Director, Paul Conner, Director of Planning & Zoning (7:30-8:00 
pm)
9A. COVER SHEET - HOUSING FORECAST AND TARGETS.PDF
9B. CCRPC HOUSING PRESENTATION.PDF
Receive an update, as set forth in the FY27 Policy Priorities and Strategies, on a 
collaboration with CCRPC on a shared Housing Needs Assessment and Housing Action 
Plan Pilot and potentially endorse this approach - Paul Conner, Director of Planning & 
Zoning (8:00-8:20 pm)
10A. COVER SHEET - HOUSING ACTION PLAN.PDF
10B. HOUSING ACTION PLAN MEMO.PDF
10C. DRAFT_FY27HOUSING_RFQ.PDF
Receive the Town Meeting TV Annual Report and Budget presentation - Jordan Mitchell, 
TMTV Co-Director of Operations & Digital Archivist CCTV / Town Meeting TV (8:20-8:35 pm)
11A. COVER SHEET - TOWN MEETING TV ANNUAL REPORT 2026.PDF
11B. TOWN MEETING TV MUNICIPAL UPDATE FY26 AND REQUEST 
FY27.PDF
Legislative Advocacy Agenda: Discuss Council priorities - Jessie Baker, City Manager, 
Nicolas Storellicastro, Deputy City Manager (8:35 -9:05 pm)
12A. COVER SHEET - LEGISLATIVE AGENDA - COUNCIL PRIORITIES.PDF
12B. LEGISLATIVE ADVOCACY AGENDA MEMO - COUNCIL PRIORITIES.PDF
Discuss the Council's goals for a vacant building and graffiti ordinance - Council Request 
(9:05-9:20 pm)
13. COVER SHEET - VACANT BUILDING AND GRAFFITI ORDINANCE.PDF
Discuss standardized communication to residents who contact the City Council and staff -
Council Request (9:20-9:35 pm)
14. COVER SHEET - COMMUNICATION WITH RESIDENTS.PDF
Discuss placing wildlife-friendly (amber) bulbs in the lights at Hubbard Park and directing 
the hours of operation of the lights - Council Request (9:35-9:50 pm)
15. COVER SHEET - LIGHTS AT HUBBARD PARK.PDF
Discuss an intended legal opinion on municipal authority to regulate building and thermal 
energy systems - Council Request (9:50-10:05 pm)
16. COVER SHEET - MUNICIPAL AUTHORITY.PDF
Discuss process and reporting improvements for high-value projects - Council Request 
(10:05-10:20 pm)
17. COVER SHEET - HIGH VALUE PROJECT REPORTING.PDF
Review the significant agenda topics below for the Council’s November 16, 2026 Council 
Meeting:(10:20-10:25 pm)
l Receive an Actuarial update on the South Burlington Pension Program 
l Receive a presentation from the Library Board of Trustees on their 5-year Strategic 
Plan 
l Approve a Legislative Advocacy Agenda for the 2027-2028 Biennium 
l Consider approving a resolution to increasing fees for parking tickets and creating 
a Parking Fund
Other Business (10:25-10:35 pm)
Consider entering into executive session pursuant to 1 V.S.A. §313(a)(1)(F) and (2) for the 
purpose of receiving confidential attorney-client communications and discussing the 
negotiation of real estate lease or purchase options, specifically 1720 Spear Street.
Consider entering into executive session pursuant to 1 V.S.A. §313(a)(1)(F) and (2) for the 
purpose of receiving confidential attorney-client communications and discussing the 
negotiation of real estate lease or purchase options, specifically the Williston Road Pump 
Station.
Adjourn
Respectfully submitted:
Jessie Baker
City Manager
Please NOTE:  All times are estimates.
